articleTitle: Short-term Load Prediction With A Combination Of Different Models
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper describes the application of different models which can be used for short-term load prediction. Seperately the nominal, weather-sensitive and residual components of the load will be predicted. Because the time series of the residuals can be consi- dered as a stationary process, the Box-Jenkins approach is used to predict the residuals. As the nominal load model uses recent load data, a special approach is ne- cessary to process weather information.

articleTitle: On The Use Of Line-current Measurements For Reliable State Estimation In Electric Power Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Current measurements areavailable in any power system measuring scheme, but few of the estimators presently being implemented are designed to employ them. This paper discusses the extension of a WLS estimator to include current measurements. The modification of the estimation algorithm itself is simple enough. The work reported here investigates the influence of current measurements on observability, the performance of the algorithm, and bad data detection probability.

articleTitle: Evaluation Of An Array Processor For Power System Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: An evaluation is given of an array processor, the AP- 120B manufactured by Floating Point Systems, Inc., for solving transient stability and similar problems. The paper describes the salient characteristics of the array processor, explains the evaluation procedure, and discusses results. With the particular host computer used, a 20 to 1 speedup in stability simulation can be obtained.

articleTitle: Simulation Of Staged Tests On The Ontario Hydro Northwestern Region
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The computer simulation of staged tests performed on the Northwestern Region of the Ontario Hydro system is discussed. Information regarding the staged tests, and subsequent duplication of the test results using a transient stability program is presented. The results of the tests and simulations indicate that accurate modelling of system loads is important, and that further work to determine appropriate load models is required.

articleTitle: A Fast Stability Program For Power Systems With Multiterminal HVDC And Static Var Comensators
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper presents a digital computer program that employs a novel, fast and efficient technique to solve transient stability problems of large scale power systems. The program has the unique features of simulating generalized (two and multi-terminal) HVDC schemes; and different types of static reactive power compensators, as well as other conventional components in a power system. Results for a complex ac/dc multimachine system under low short circuit ratio conditions are presented.

articleTitle: On-line Computer Monitoring Of Complex Power System Stabtlity Limits
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Operation of a Power System which is highly constrained by stability considerations, generator rejection schemes and security standards requires complex control and operating strategies. This paper presents on-line computer software and systems which were used to allow Power System Control Centre Operators to monitor and control such a stability constrained Power System.

articleTitle: Distribution System Design Using Computer Graphics Technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper describes models for computer-aided distribution system design. It comprises primary distribution master planning, primary feeder routing, and secondary distribution system planning. The primary master planning is concerned with the preliminary location analysis of electric distribution facilities for planned development or redevelopment of areas. The purpose is to provide and evaluate goal design of subtransmission and primary substation system on basis of projected land use. The primary feeder and secondary system models are concerned with the more detailed distribution network synthesis at stages when more precise data about area growth and loads are available.

articleTitle: The On-line Equipment Limit Monitoring Facility Of The Ontario Hydro Data Acquisition And Computer System
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: To keep pace with growing system complexity, Ontario Hydro placed a Data Acquisition and Computer System (DACS) in- service on June 11, 1976, at its system Control Centre. The facility monitors over 2,800 status points and 2,400 analog points every two seconds and presents this information on CRTs and a system mimic diagram. in addition to this constantly updated picture of the power system, the Control Supervisors are provided with a set of software packages to assist them in achieving a secure and economical operating pattern. To assist the Control Supervisor in preserving the system's security, an Equipment Limit Monitoring (ELM) facility was provided to determine if the Bulk Electricity System (BES.) equipment is being operated within ampacity limits both on a continuous basis and in the face of contingencies.

articleTitle: Power System Programming In Pascal
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: PASCAL, a relative newcomer among high level programming languages, is compared with FORTRAN for power system programming applications. PASCAL is briefly described and fea- tures of interest for power applications are pointed out. A sparsity-oriented short circuit analysis program is developed in both languages and comparisons are made of their time and storage requirements. Also, an informal comparison is made of less quantifiable items, such as length of source code, readability, ease of coding and debuging and ease of maintenance. Based on use of a rather unsophisticated PASCAL compiler, FORTRAN shows a speed and memory advantage of 2 or 3 to 1 . Part of this is probably inherent in the languages, but most of the differences could be elimi nated by some simple extensions to the PASCAL language and changes in the compilers. PASCAL shows definite advantages in terms of the less tangible measures. This paper points out that PASCAL-based languages are going to be widely used in military and other systems and suggests that it deserves serious consideration for power system applications.

articleTitle: A Medium And Short Term Load Forecasting Model For Electrical Industry
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: In order to define daily, weekly and yearly generation and transmission schedules it is necessary to have available a fo- recast of power demand respectively for the next 24 hours, 7 days, 52 weeks. In this paper a description is given of a model used for power demand forecast either for short and medium term. Results are shown of an experimental application of the forecasting model to the hourly power demand of an actual electrical System, which is part of the ENEL system. Some activities are at last illustrated, which are in a development phase at ENEL, and which are oriented to the definition of load forecasting models to be used in scheduling, advance dispat- ching and on-line dispatching phases.

articleTitle: Coherency Based Dynamic Equivalent Application Experience - Eastern Us Data Base
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The results of calculating an equivalent for transient stability studies from a data base for the large, tightly coupled eastern US power system are presented. The method was based on generator coherency, the tendency for groups of generators to swing together. Previously developed computer programs were expanded to accommodate system sizes up to about 8,000 buses. Program input parameters controlling the calculations were varied somewhat to determine their effect. The final result was an equivalent which was significantly smaller than the original system and reasonably accurate.

articleTitle: Optimization Of A Very Large Hydroelectric System By Network Flow Techniques With Additional Constraints
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: A method and a computing program are described in this paper for optimal daily scheduling of hydraulically cascaded power plants with dual pumping and generation operating modes, in order to supply a given diagram vs. time of the active power. The program schedules every pumping or generation plant in order to minimize water consumption and satisfy the given generation diagram, with due consideration to the actual characteristics of hydraulic machinery and to the hydraulic constraints. The chosen procedure to solve the above problem, which is one of non-linear optimization with many integer variables, resorts to a suitable piecewise linearization. After this, the continuous problem is solved with the techniques of optimization on network flow with additional constraints. Finally, the mixed integer problem is solved using Tomlin's branch and bound method.

articleTitle: Interactions Between Torsional Vibrations Of Large Turboalternators And Electric Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The paper deals with the problem of torsional vibrations on the shaft of modern large turboalternators. The theoretical development is essentially based upon the definition of electrical analogues both for the mechanical part (machine's rotor) and for the electric power system as viewed from the machine's ports. Practical simplified computing procedures are also derived; their validity and advantages are examined and illustrated via realistic data of an existing system.

articleTitle: The Application Of A Database System To On-line Security Assessment In An EHV-network
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Two main reasons exist for the incorporation of a data base management system into a power system security assessment package. They are: i) to enable the use of a modular structure in the software design. This leads to an ease of extension and maintainability of the software as required by computer system and power system developments. ii) to provide a standardised data structure for the many varied system activities having common data requirements. The application discussed in this paper involves the monitoring and security checking of an EHV network and the system is implemented on a PDP 11/70 pro- cess computer. The particular functions described involve: i) data acquisition (ii) network topology determination (iii) network observability determination (iv) state estimation (v) limit checking (vi) operators load flow. The features of particular interest include the structuring of the data base to optimise the performance of the various software functions, and the interface mechanism between the various, often independent, activities in the system. The method of initialising and updating the data base from cards and/or terminal is described, and the facilities for concurrently studying both real-time and simulation systems are Outlined. A number of data base oriented utilities are mentioned which support the on-line operation and software development and which assist in maintaining and debugging the system.

articleTitle: A Computer Based System For EHV Line Monitoring And Control
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: A real-time digital data-acquisition and processing system has been operating continuously since late May 78 in an Hydro-Quebec 735 kV substation. This paper describes the actual implementation and reports the operating experience. The prototype was developped in the first stage of a research project on computer-based line protection. The software is designed to accomodate (i) relaying algorithm (ii) auto verification (iii) self-evaluation and (iv) communication functions. All these functions are performed on line. Relaying algorithm consists of a one-cycle Fourier analysis and a continuous calculation of impedances. The sampling rate is controlled by the computer to synchronize to the power system frequency. Upon detection of a perturbation, five to fifty cycles of rel evant voltage and current waveform samples are "frozen" and transmitted via a phone link to IREQ main computer for permanent storage and further processing. Performances of the protection algorithm are evaluated auto matically against the actual protection system. An auto-answer modem allows the control of the remote system.

articleTitle: Bus Voltage And Injection Measurements In The Aep State Estimator
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: In the original formulation of the AEP estimator, only measurements of complex power flows in transmission lines and transformers were processed and a reference voltage measurement was used deterministically (1). This meas- urement set permitted the formulation of a relatively simple and computationally fast algorithm. This paper discusses the formulation for including voltage and injection measurements in the present algorithm. One important aspect of the paper is the expansion of the measurement set while preserving the basic char- acteristics of the original algorithm. The paper also discusses the detection and identification of erroneous measurements as well as the calculation of confidence limits from the expanded measurement set.

articleTitle: Synchronous Machine Initialization For Unbalanced Network Conditions Within An Electromagnetic Transients Program
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The Electromagnetic Transients Program (EMTP) offers two quite different algorithms for the representation of synchronous machine dynamics. The original [1) uses compensation [2], while the second [3, 4] is based on a Thevenin equivalent of the generator. It is shown that positive sequence initialization is inadequate if the electric network is even just slightly unbalanced (e.g., untransposed lines). Two new initialization procedures which also account for negative (and possibly zero) sequence armature quantities are now being used. Even cases of gross imbalance (e.g., one phase open) can now be handled easily. Sample digital computer calculations are presented, including simulations of the IEEE subsynchronous resonance (SSR) benchmark model using large time-steps.

articleTitle: Data Definition And Management Techniques For Interactive Geo-facility Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: All utility systems face the problem of producing and maintaining accurate records on their geographic facilities -- those facilities located throughout a geographic area for the purpose of providing service to the utility's customers. These records commonly include both alphanumeric and graphic information, such as distribution maps, circuit diagrams and design specifications. Some early attempts to apply computers to cope with this problem have attacked a single piece -- for example, map drafting systems have been designed to faithfully reproduce and edit the final graphic report (maps). However, in such systems, the alphanumeric data vital for engineering and design calculations are often lost. This paper describes a comprehensive geo-facility system. In this system, data management techniques are used to preserve the relationships between a facility and other facilities, and between a facility and the various components of its description. The description of a facility is developed using data definition techniques for both facility attributes and graphic presentation. The geo-facility workstation supports an x-y tablet input device. A variety of specialized operations can be invoked by pointing to menus located on the tablet. The design of these menus and the relationship of these menus to the facility definition requires additional data definition. The interaction of the various definition and management functions described above is illustrated with a sample design session.

articleTitle: Mathematical - Programming Solution of Optimum Dispatch
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: When solving the optimum-dispatch problem with mathematical programming techniques, powers or voltages may be used as variables. It is shown that the second approach makes for lower strorage and computational requirements, and that selection of the starting accuracy and its subsequence adaptation is decisive for convergence. Results are reported as evidence of the correctness of these conclusions.

articleTitle: An Efficient State Estimation Method Through Transformations
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Result of tests on a radial system show the importance of voltage magnitude and zero injection measurements in the identifica- tion of gross errors in the state estimation problem. Computational efficiency is enhanced by the use of a transformed set of measure- ments. Zero injections are handled such that the matrix used in the estimation process has an admittance like structure. All voltage magnitude measurements are included as random variables and no deterministic voltages are used. Weighting factors are analysed and appropriate values are recommended in order to obtain adequate convergence characteristics. The filtering capabilities of the estimator are tested and the results obtained discussed. Result of extensive tests on two systems part of the 230/400 KV Mexican Network are summarized in tables. Line flow and voltage measurement gross errors were simulated and the importance of the location of measured nodal quantities in the identification process reported. Common error identification problems between radial and meshed systems are also discussed.

articleTitle: Input-output Processing Of On-line Contingency Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The requirements and design of the input- output processing of an on-line steady state contingency analysis program for a power system control center are outlined in this paper. A method is described to accommodate the secondary changes in the power system configuration that may be caused by the input contingencies that have to be studied by this program. The scheme utilizes a technique to quickly detect contingencies that produce secondary changes, the presence of which requires the use of the topology processor before solving for the power flows. The output processing consists mainly of ranking the output data so that only a reasonable amount of information has to be displayed to the operator. In addition, the violation of equipment limits indicated by the program are tracked over time by using an equipment violation matrix which can be stored very efficiently using several different techniques.

articleTitle: Solution Of The Load Flow Problem By A Parallel Optimization Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The Load Flow problem is treated as a minimization problem and is solved using a parallel nangradient optimization procedure similar to the one suggested by Chazan and Miranker. The algorithm is described and test case results are presented. A speed-up nearly equal to q is possible if a parallel computer with q processors is used for the solution of the problem.

articleTitle: Computer Network Design Concepts For Tke Capco Pool
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The coordination of operating functions affecting economy and security in a power pool requires communications among member companies and between member companies and the pool office. A study of the operating requirements of the CAPCO pool has resulted in the development of concepts for the design of a two-level information and control hierarchy consisting of four company control centers at one level and a pool center at the second level. This paper shall describe the philosophy and design requirements of the computer network which would connect the two-level hierarchy.

articleTitle: Software Modules And Data Structures for Process-computer Application In The Grid Automation Sector
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: With complex automation systems controlled by process computers the main problems of effort, costs, implementation time, complexity and therefore the need to use highly qualified manpower arise in the software sector. Because of this fact, standard software systems are of considerable importance for the reduction of software costs and implementation times, transfer of know-how and also as a guide for the quick and clear definition of the problems to be solved. This paper reports on software modules, data structures and communication routines used in a standard software system for grid automation.

articleTitle: Reliable Error Recovery In Distributed Computer Control Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The critical nature of computer control applications such as electric power generation and distribution has led to tightly coupled computer systems in which manually. multiple processors and devices may be electronically switched into various configurations for backup purposes. By distributing the tasks into separate but communicating modules, overall system reliability and availability may be achieved with less complex hardware Furthermore, distribution of the time critical tasks leads to less complex software. Error recovery in such a system is complicated not by the distribution of the application tasks but by the distribution of the data base shared among the tasks. Error recovery techniques are discussed, especially their effect an the resulting loading of the communication channels.

articleTitle: Three Phase Simulation Of The Dynamic Interaction Between Synchronous Generators And Power Systems Using The Continuous Systems Modeling Program (CSMP III)
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper presents the convenient features of the Continuous Systems Modeling Program (CSMP III) in developing of three-phase power system dynamic performance. A modified large resistor interface between the synchronous generator and the network is developed. A method of computing the initial conditions of the machie including the more common situation of unbalanced conditions at the generator terminals is suggested. The necessary mathematical models of the synchronous generator and the various power system network components are provided for completness. Examples of load rejection and single-pole switching applications are included to demonstrate the simulation capabilities using CSMP III.

articleTitle: Costing Of Outages, Deratings and Operating Reserves Using Real-time Data
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: A computerized algorithm which is capable of evaluating the costs of-outages, deratings and operating reserves on an hourly basis is presented in this paper. This program is designed to handle a large power system and to use actual operations data so as to maintain a high degree of accuracy. The technique used in this algorithm also strives to minimize the computer time required by making use of a priority list of units as opposed to performing economic dispatches. This tool is potentially valuable to production personnel in justifying additional costs for maintenance and equipment. The program promises to be a means of increasing the effectiveness of planning, production and operations personnel in the decision process.

articleTitle: A Digital Controller For Testing Control Strategy At Power Plants
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper describes the software and hardware of a programmable digital controller that was designed to enable the power system engineer to derive parameters and control strategies with a maximum degree of flexibility and efficiency during field test situations at power plants. Many test situations arise, in practical situations, where a person is attempting to determine suitable feedback parameters prior to establishing the "frozen" form of the analog, or digital, controller that will be permanently installed. In many cases prior theoretical calculations and simulation studies have enabled the designer to obtain "ball park" parameters for the controller and what is required is a further fine-tuning on-site to establish confidence that the controller, to be permanently installed, will do an adequate job. The programmable digital controller described in this paper has been tested extensively during field tests at power plants where studies were being conducted on the effect of power system stabilizer feedback to damp out local mode and inter-tie mode oscillations. The digital controller incorporates many attractive features that make it compatible with power system security. These include high impedance buffering on input and output of the digital controller, and redundant software and hardware limiting on the controller to avoid overdriving the critical control loops of the generator. One of the drawbacks of "off the shelf" microprocessors, or minicomputers in the low end price range, is the cycle time that severely limits the number of mathematical operations (multiplications, additions, etc) that can be done between A/D samples in the control algorithm. The digital controller described in this paper utilizes a microprocessor system with modifications and hardware improvements so that the digital controller is able to work in the fast feed back loops of the power plant with fairly complex and high order controllers simulated in the controller. Finally, a sample of some of the field test results obtained with the digital controller is included in the paper.

articleTitle: The Value Of Model Accuracy And Validation To The Utility Engineer
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The importance or validation studies and tests to the utility engineer is discussed. Methods of validation and some of the problems associated with each method are described. Examples of validation studies made at PGandE are presented.

articleTitle: Computer Model For Assessing Domestic Heat Pump Loads
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The assessment of heat pump impact on power system planning and operation, must be made with detailed analysis of the interrelationship between heat pump system heated house - climate. X computer model to calculate heat pump loads is described, which also can be used to analyse the results from monitored, data of several heat pump configurations and different climate regions. Output from the program is presented as daily load curves and yearly load duration curves for both coincident and non-coincident demand.

articleTitle: Enel Power Generation And Transmission Control System
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: ENEL, the Italian Electricity Board, has planned to set up a hierarchical computer system to control the Italian power generation and transmis sion system by 1981-82, The power generation and transmission control (PGTC) system has a multi level structure which consists of the National Control Center (NCC) located in Rome, eight Area Control Centers (ACC), Remote Control Centers (RCC) and Remote Terminal Units (RTU) at the stations. The paper describes the control functions, the control centers and the hierarchical structure require ments. Emphasis is given to the operational proce dures used in normal conditions and to the measures provided to cope with failures in the computer system.

articleTitle: Emergency State Control For Power Station Operating Using Process Computer
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Emergency state control is an important research topic which presently receives a lot of attention [1]. For this operating condition the design of a digital power station control is discussed in this paper for a specific model using pseudo-frequency domain analysis in this manner it is possible to derive DDC units for each control loop such that prespecified step responses of the process variables are obtained. Furthermore it is possible to guarantee that the admissible rates of change are fully exploited without exceeding them. Using interactive computing methods in the pseudo-frequency domain results in digital control structures which widely differ from the present ones. Since the numerical implementation is straight forward it seems realistic that the improved power reserve and stability behaviour may substantially contribute towards emergency state control.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis And Reliability Calculations In Digital Protection Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Digital systems with one-way components can be represented by acyclic digraphs when analysing the input-output terminal reliability. A 4-step algorithm based on a combinational approach is presented to calculate the probability and frequency of failure of alternative configurations for digital protection systems, using the minimal cut-set approach to system reliability. Generally the lack of proper component data prohiblts a particular reliability evaluation, so a general algorithmic procedure is presented for a sensitivity analysis which allows to improve the reliability of the system through the knowledge of the component parameters that have a critical effect. The algorithms are illustrated by examining two practical applications.

articleTitle: Digital Simulation And System Model Verification For The San Diego System Disturbance
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: On March 8, 1979, San Diego Gas & Electric Company experienced a major system disturbance which resulted in system islanding and interruption of service to approximately two-thirds of it load and half of its electric customers. A task force was immediately established to determine: a) the cause of the disturbance and its duration, b) the events which occurred during the transient period which led to system seperation and, c) the procedures used to reconnect th system and restore service to customers. This paper concentrates on the simulation of events which occurred during the transient period and discusses the accuracy and validity of certain models used in the system simulation. The paper also discusses how the computer simulation, in conjunction with recorded and observed data, was utilized to determine the timing of some of the switching operations

articleTitle: Computer-aided Data Collection For Distribution Planning
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Circuit connections for electric distribution networks are often recorded only on geographic maps of the service area. While record systems of this type are adequate for manual usage, they do not permit computer analysis since the data is not available in tabular form. In the past, the major hindrance to creating tabular files from such maps has been the large amount of time and human effort required. This research demonstrates a solution to this problem that utilizes an electronic digitizer in conjunction with a minicomputer. using this system, circuit data and transformer connections from separate maps can be digitized electronically and superimposed on a master map by the computer. The computer then creates tabular data files from these digitized maps. Examples taken from the Toledo Edison system are included.

articleTitle: Review Of Linear Programming Applied To Power System Rescheduling
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Linear and related programming methods have application in transmission planning, security dispatch and emergency control of power systems. With a large still-growing body of literature on the subject, this paper offers a short review of the available LP approaches, techniques and formulations, with due emphasis on state-of-the-art versions. The differences between primal and dual methods and sparse and nonsparse formulations are exposed, and various important techniques such as relaxation, upper bounding and separable programming are dealt with. Thus the paper attempts to provide some clarification of the main fundamental analytical and computational, issues involved in the design of an LP-based method for the rescheduling of power-system operation.

articleTitle: A Microcomputer Based Symmetrical Component Distance Relay
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper summarizes the newly developed concept of a Symmetrical Component Distance Relay (SCDR). Digital computer implementation of the SCDR and a micro computer based hardware system suitable for this task is described. Salient features of the relay algorithm are given, and laboratory tests of the SCDR program described. Field testing of the micro- computer based SCER is planned for the Spring of 1979.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Program For Computing Coherency-based Dynamic Equivalents
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper describes the method and associated computer programs for calculating dynamic equivalents of large synchronously interconnected systems. Tests of the method have been performed on large scale representations of both the Eastern U.S. (1159 generators, 5838 buses) and Western U.S. (337 generators, 1308 buses) interconnected systems. The method is highly efficient and is capable of developing dynamic equivalents which provide significant reductions in system model size while maintaining acceptable accuracy.

articleTitle: An Assessment Of Computer Technology For Large Scale Power System Simulation
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: A true technological explosion has taken place in the computer hardware industry in the last few years. Words such as parallel processing, vector processors, array processors, pipelined machines, "number crunching", and megaflops (Millions of FLoating-point OPerations per Second) are heard regularly. Computer manufacturers have responded to the needs of specific groups requiring, above all else, high speed arithmetic capability. The result is a host of new machines which are called in this paper "vector processors". This paper will assess the applicability of vector processors to power flow and transient stability simulation programs and will indicate how these pro- grams should be organized to run efficiently on these new machines. The approach taken will be to survey the entire class of vector processors available now and in the near future, to attempt to raise the reported low efficiency of sparsity-coded programs for large vector processors by reorganizing their sparse structure, and to show how the most time-consuming parts of power system simulation can be "vectorized" for these machines.

articleTitle: A Two-stage Approach To Solving Large-scale Optimal Power Flows
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: A two stage optimization algorithm is developed for the solution of the large-scale optimal power flow (OPF) problem. The solution scheme is arrived at by exploiting the structural properties of the OPF problem formulation, including the physical characteristics of its variables. The algorithm incorporates certain features of the generalized reduced gradient and the penalty function methods. At each iteration a modified reduced gradient is used to provide a direction of movement. The use of penalty functions in the optimization is kept at a minimum. The generalized reduced gradient ideas are adapted in such a way that a routine power flow is used in the optimization. Numerical results of test cases including a 1410 bus system are given.

articleTitle: Application Of An Array Processor For Power System Network Computations
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The application of an array processor to solution of power system network equations is discussed and results from its performance evaluation are presented. The particular array processor which was studied performs network solutions several times faster than general purpose large mainframe digital computers and is available at a fraction of the cost. It has an immediate application for decreasing the computer costs and improving the responsiveness of programs which are used in power system planning and operations.

articleTitle: A Reevaluation Of The Normal Operating State Control Of The Power System Using Computer Control And System Theory*
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The economic dispatch and load frequency control problem is approached as a design for digital computer control with system theoretic foundations from scratch but utilizes the ingenious insights of the past 30 years of practice. In Part I of the paper, an estimation process is proposed which gives a much tighter estimate of the area load excess (ALE) over the scheduled load than the traditional area control error (ACE) while it also provides an extrapolated es- timate into the future and an estimate of the turbine power at each unit. The latter is needed for unit control. Part II** introduces a three step algorithm to generate extrapolated target curves for the individual units to follow for economically matching the area load demand throughout the day.

articleTitle: The Use Of A Multiprocessor Network For The Transient Stability Problem
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper examines the possibility of using a dedicated multiprocessor network to do the step-by-step computations needed in the digital simulation of the dynamic response of a large power system. This multiprocessor network would use a general purpose digital computer for the input and output. It is found that over 97% of the computations for a typical 1723-bus, 396-machine, stability study could be done in parallel. Approximately 30% of the computation time is spent solving the network equations, I = YE. Various algorithms for this part of the solution and ways of scheduling the work assignments to the processors are discussed.

articleTitle: Power System Control Center Concepts
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper presents the thinking behind the evolution of control center design at Control Data Corporation. Various aspects of the present day control center are discussed, together with the limitations and compromises that are needed to meet a complex set of requirements. The emphasis is on the present state of the art as represented by control centers that have been recently installed or are in production. Trends for the future are discussed as providing for the next decade may be the greatest problem in system design. The explosive growth in the number and complexity of functions performed in control centers has forced an evolution away from a single processor approach to distributed processing systems, which must be more responsive to the needs of applications programs, both from a development and real-time usage standpoint. In planning for the expected life of the computer systems, it is important that the system accom- modate horizontal growth -- more RTU's, CRT's, bigger data bases, etc., as well as vertical growth -- new functions which must be performed and which cannot be anticipated today.

articleTitle: Lotdys Analysis Of August 1973 Gulf Coast Area Power System Disturbance
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: This paper presents results of research sponsored by EPRI on long term power system dynamics conducted by General Electric under contract RP764-2 with support from Southern Company Services, Inc. An analysis of a major power system disturbance was made by digital computer simulation of the interacting dynamics of power plants, electrical transmission systems, and connected customer loads. The incident under examination occurred on Tuesday morning, August 7, 1973 in the southern Alabama and Mississippi and western Florida portions of the Southern electric system and resulted in the formation of an electrical island. The seven minute simulation of the Gulf Coast area electrical island was made to: 0 Test and validate the computer program LOTDYS, 0 Explore the effect of alternate simulation data to improve the accuracy of the simulation, 0 Provide further insight and information on this specific incident, 0 Identify and make improvements in analytic methods and data acquisition and estimation methods. The simulation of the disturbance was compared to disturbance records and a good match over a two minute period was obtained between the records and the simulation results. This match was obtained by use of conventional electrical system data supplied by Southern Company Services and typical data for load and prime mover characteristics obtained from a prior EPRI long term dynamics project.(l) In the period after one minute of island operation, the effects of steam plan safety valves and boiler fire trip and restart were found to be significant; LOTOYS was modified to add models of these effects in order to obtain a match to plant pressure chart records. In the period following the first two minutes of the island operation, operator actions and changes in connected customer load were found to be significant; a fair match was obtained by incorporating assumed manual run back of generation and assumed values of load pickup rate.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Prediction For Economic Dispatch Of Generation
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: A set of procedures and algorithms are developed for short-term (1-3 hours) electric power system load prediction. The short-term load predictors provide "look ahead" capability for an economic dispatch that coordinates predicted load changes with the rate-of- response capability of generation units. The short- term load prediction also enables valve-point loading of generation units. The predictor models are estimated empirically. Test results are given for the predictor models applied to actual loads of an electric utility.

articleTitle: On Line Detection And Recording Of Major Disturbances In The Enel Power System
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The main features of a special purpose data acquition system, named RIPES , for on-line detection and recording of major electromechanic disturbances in the ENEL system, are describ- ed. The description also includes the specifications referring to the classes of disturbances that must be detected, to the modelling of the dominant dynamic phenomena to be analysed and to the electrical quantities to be measured. Examples of disturbances detected by the RIPES system are reported.

articleTitle: Interactive Graphic Inquiry System For Electric Generation Planning
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: An interactive graphic inquiry system for use in electric generation planning is presented. The computer program couples extensive hard and soft copy graphic capabilities, function analysis, and other features with a complete data base needed for comprehensive energy planning studies. Easy inquiry of any data base parameter values on a random access basis is possible, with the option of modifying or updating any desired variable. It is simple enough for even non-technical people to use yet has the power, flexibility and efficiency needed by experienced energy planners for rapid, high-quality evaluations. It has been integrated into a multi-computer network that can perform fast, comprehensive analyses of generation planning questions at a very low user cost.

articleTitle: Integrated Program Package For Power System Studies
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: A number of digital computer programs are currently available for power system studies. These programs are being used to model networks of increasing size and complexity and the provision of effective data management facilities has become crucial to their successful implementation. The paper describes an integrated interactive computer package for power system analysis ("POWSYS"). This package was developed at the Electricity Supply Commission (South Africa) and has been used extensively by its planning and operating engineers for a number of years. The package features a common file structure of network data and results which is accessed by a set of power system analysis programs. These programs provide the major digital simulation capabilities required to study the behaviour of power systems under both steady state and transient conditions. A simple free-format command language enables the user to control the sequence of studies interactively and to utilize the built in data management and reporting facilities provided. The package is open-ended and the addition of new commands and analysis programs is easily accomplished. The paper will describe the main features and facilities afforded by the data management software and will giveabrief overview of the analysis programs currently implemented.

articleTitle: Daily Fossil Fuel Management
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The problem of daily fossil fuel management for electrical generators has become more complex with the use of fuels of different types, from different sources and costs at each generating unit. In addition, physical constraints and contractual limitations may impose upper and lower bounds on the amounts of each fuel that are available. The problem is to minimize the total cost of fuel by choice of the amount of each type fuel used for each unit in each operating period of the day subject to the constraints on fuel availability. Four algorithms have been developed and are presented. While the basis or strategy used in each varies, the results are fairly close. The correct choice of algorithm used will depend on the ease of solution and the ability to implement the strategy through actual generating plant instrumentation and control.

articleTitle: Introduction Of Security Constraints In A Probabilistic Model For Estimating The Supply Reliability Of Power Transmission Systems (the Mexico Model)
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: The MEXICO model is used at E.D.F. to estimate the supply reliability in planning studies of H.V. or E.H.V. power transmission systems. It permits the determination of the expected annual unsupplied energy taking into account Consumption uncertainties, in addition of the uncertainties on the availability of generation and transmission equipment, - Security constraints in the unsupplied demand computing algorithm, i.e., the transfer limits of lines and transformers to be satisfied under both normal and emergency operating conditions.

articleTitle: Real-time Energy Control
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: Today's energy control centers must meet ever-increasing real-time demands. Rising fuel costs and the operation of power systems closer to operating constraints are motivating dispatchers to continuously search for the best operational balance of economics and security. Nine modern centers design- ed to meet these increased real-time demands are surveyed. The major elements of a Leeds & Northrup Energy Control System --- computer subsystem, data acquisition equipment, man/machine interface, application programs, and dispatcher training facilities -- are reviewed.

articleTitle: Interactive Load Flow Utilizing Tabular Display Format
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: An interactive load flow program designed for use on relatively inexpensive, black and white, alphanumeric CRT terminals, such as those typically available for time sharing use, is described in this paper. The program allows on-line recall of previously saved data, interactive data entry and modification, on-line solution of the load flow problem, and interactive display of the solved case. Hard copy output ranging from "snapshots" of individual display screens to full printed output of the solved case may also be obtained. In addition, load flow cases may be prepared for solution in the background using an optional batch job spin-off feature. The program may also be used to recall and display the results of cases which have been solved and saved either during previous interactive sessions or as the result of execution of background jobs in the batch job stream. The program contains code for execution in both the interactive and batch environments.

articleTitle: Regional Analysis Models And Interactive Computer Graphics At Doe Laboratories : Their Use In Power System Planning
publicationTitle: IEEE Conference Proceedings Power Industry Computer Applications Conference, 1979. PICA-79.
abstract: A survey has been made of regional analysis models and interactive computer graphic systems at three Department Of Energy (DOE) laboratories. Specific practices were studied and a report was prepared describing applications, data bases, and interactive computer graphic systems. Many of these products have been applied to the study of electric utility systems and could he used for planning by the electric power industry. This paper describes the view of power system planning held by researchers at DOE laboratories, the nature of the models which have been developed, the types of studies which have been performed, and the utilization of computer resources. Particular attention has been given to the role of computer graphics in these studies. A comparison has been made with Perspectives and practices of the electric power industry. The paper emphasizes DOE applicationse data bases and computer graphic systems. Applications include: Power plant siting; routing of transmission lines; air quality, water quaIity and land use modelling; and analysis of the esthetice biomedical, fuel use and regional resource impact of different electric industry decisions. Many of these applications falI outside the historic conception of electric power system planning, but they deal with matters which utiIity companies are increasingly required to consider in their generation and transmission planning.
